findings.claim: The assessment bases the brand-source hierarchy on source files that the packet marks as missing, so downstream analysis/plan would rely on an unverified source of truth.
findings.evidence: Assessment says precedence #1 is `know-me-system/docs/knowme-ui-ux-standard.md` and precedence #3 includes `desktop/src/shared/components/KnowMeLogo.tsx`, but `cited_paths` reports `MISSING  know-me-system/docs/knowme-ui-ux-standard.md` and `MISSING  desktop/src/shared/components/KnowMeLogo.tsx`.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run assessment against accessible brand sources, quote only paths that exist in the packet/repository or explicitly mark unavailable sources as unresolved inputs instead of resolved precedence.

findings.claim: The assessment does not assess the goal requirement to keep WCAG contrast passing beyond two isolated color concerns.
findings.evidence: Goal: `Verify brand fidelity visually at 320/768/1024/1440 in both themes and keep build, tests, lint and WCAG contrast passing`. Assessment's Goal Progress item 7 says `no visual test harness; lint and tsc already failing`, while contrast appears only as open risks for `Primary-button text on ember` and `Faint-text value conflict`; there is no current contrast gap analysis for existing surfaces, tokens, or light/dark themes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a WCAG contrast assessment section covering current token pairs and major UI surfaces in both themes, or explicitly state that contrast was not audited and must be a planning task.
